rows.name: TRON_HEAP_SHADOW
rows.values: Exactly `1` turns the shadow map on. The code compares the text with `strcmp`. Any other text, such as `true`, is off. No message is logged.
rows.default: Unset: the shadow map is off, unless the option `--heap-shadow` is given.
rows.effect: The arena allocator (`pos_heap_v2`, the default allocator for hugepage memory) keeps one record for each live allocation, with the requested size and the caller addresses. Each free checks the pointer and the size against the record. A mismatch aborts the process.
rows.notes: `--heap-shadow` does the same, on the command line or in `SYSTEM_CONFIG`. The variable cannot turn that option off. No effect when `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR` selects the legacy heap. Check: the log line `pos_heap_setup: using arena allocator (pos_heap_v2) with shadow map`.

rows.name: TRON_HWATTN_COMPOUND_SPLIT
rows.values: Integer, parsed with `std::atol`. The code does not use the result.
rows.effect: No effect. The code reads the variable, computes a flag and discards the flag.
rows.notes: A source comment says that the variable is intentionally ignored. The read happens only when hardware attention is active for the model.

evidence.quote: // TRON_HWATTN_COMPOUND_SPLIT is intentionally ignored: compound passes can

rows.name: TRON_HWATTN_EARLY_LAUNCH_MIN_B
rows.values: Decimal integer of 1 or more, digits `0` to `9` only. Unit: tokens in one minibatch. Empty text, `0`, a sign, a space or a letter is rejected.
rows.default: Unset: 4 tokens. Empty: rejected like an invalid value.
rows.effect: Sets the smallest minibatch that launches hardware attention early. A minibatch is a group of tokens that one forward pass computes together. At or above this size, hardware attention launches before the keys and values of the current token are saved, and below this size it launches after.
rows.notes: The check runs at the first use, in a forward pass. A rejected value logs `invalid TRON_HWATTN_EARLY_LAUNCH_MIN_B` and aborts the process. The value does not change which operations use hardware attention. Perfetto events of the category `hwattention-detail` show it as `min_b`.

rows.name: TRON_HWATTN_HEAD_TILING
rows.values: Integer, parsed with `atoi`. A result above 0 forces head tiling on. Any other set value forces it off: `0`, a negative number, or text that is not a number.
rows.default: Unset: each FPGA card decides from its bitfile: on for project 01 or 03 with version 05.09 or later. Empty: forced off.
rows.effect: Forces head tiling on or off for every FPGA card and skips the bitfile check. Head tiling applies when a context is too long for one hardware attention pass over all heads. The card then gets one command that handles fewer heads per pass, not several commands.
rows.notes: When set, the log shows once `HW attention: TRON_HWATTN_HEAD_TILING=<value> forces the feature ON` or `OFF`. Words such as `true` force it off. The value is read once per process. No command-line flag sets it.

rows.name: TRON_HW_SAMPLER
rows.values: Exactly `1` or `true` turns the sampler on. The comparison is case-sensitive. Any other text is off. No message is logged.
rows.default: Unset: off. No sampler thread is created. A trace holds no counters of the category `hw`.
rows.effect: Turns on the hardware sampler. When a trace session starts, the process creates one sampler thread. While the trace records the category `hw`, the thread reads CPU temperature, CPU frequency and package power from `/sys` and writes them to the Perfetto trace as counters.
rows.notes: It has an effect only when a trace starts. The script `perfetto/grant-rapl-read` accepts the same 2 values. It then uses `sudo` to give all local users read access to the RAPL files (CPU energy counters) under `/sys/class/powercap`. Package power needs that access.

evidence.quote: // The sampler is OFF unless TRON_HW_SAMPLER=1 (or `true`). Enabling it costs a

rows.name: TRON_HW_SAMPLER_ALL_SENSORS
rows.values: Exactly `1` or `true` turns it on. The comparison is case-sensitive. Any other text is off. No message is logged.
rows.default: Unset: off. For each CPU socket the trace gets the package temperature and the minimum, average and maximum of the other temperature sensors.
rows.effect: Adds one temperature counter for every CPU temperature sensor to the trace, next to the summary counters of each socket. The counter name is `<driver> socket<N> <label> (C)`.
rows.notes: It has an effect only when `TRON_HW_SAMPLER` turns the hardware sampler on. The sampler thread reads it once, at its first sample. A source comment gives 26 sensors for a server with 2 EPYC CPUs and about 146 sensors for 2 Granite Rapids CPUs.

evidence.quote: // This is what TRON_HW_SAMPLER_ALL_SENSORS=1 adds to the trace; the aggregates

rows.name: TRON_HW_SAMPLER_INTERVAL_MS
rows.values: Integer number of milliseconds, parsed with `atoll`. Only a result above 0 is used. `0`, a negative number and text that is not a number select the default.
rows.effect: Sets the wait between two samples of the hardware sampler.
rows.notes: It has an effect only when `TRON_HW_SAMPLER` turns the hardware sampler on. The sampler thread reads it once, when the thread starts. Text that starts with a number uses that number: `50ms` means 50 ms. No log line shows the value.

rows.name: TRON_HW_SAMPLER_SYSFS_ROOT
rows.values: Path of a directory with the layout of `/sys`. Any non-empty text is used without a check. Empty text counts as unset.
rows.effect: Replaces `/sys` as the root of every file that the hardware sampler reads. The sampler reads `class/hwmon`, `class/powercap` and `devices/system/cpu` under this root.
rows.notes: A source note says that tests use it to point the sampler at an artificial directory tree. It has an effect only when `TRON_HW_SAMPLER` turns the hardware sampler on. A root without sensor files gives no counters and no error.

rows.name: TRON_LATCH_WATCHDOG
rows.values: Integer number of seconds, parsed with `atoi`. A positive result turns the watchdog on. `0` and text that is not a number leave it off.
rows.default: Unset: off. No watchdog thread is created.
rows.effect: Each latch arena (the latches of one model state) starts one watchdog thread. A latch is a counter that threads wait on during a forward pass. Every N seconds the thread writes an info log entry `Latch states:` with the count and name of every latch.
rows.notes: A negative number also starts the thread. The thread then logs about every 100 ms. The thread pins itself to CPU 0. The CMake CI workflow sets `60` for all its jobs. No command-line flag sets it.

rows.name: TRON_LIVE_TOKEN_LIMIT
rows.values: Integer, parsed with `atoi`. A working value is 1 or more. Unit: tokens that one forward pass computes. Text that is not a number counts as `0`.
rows.default: Unset: 100000000 tokens (100 million). Empty: counts as `0`.
rows.effect: Limits the number of tokens that one forward pass (one run of the model over a group of tokens) of a scheduler computes. At the limit the scheduler stops adding tokens to the pass and reports that the pass did not schedule everything.
rows.notes: With `0` or a negative number, no token enters a pass. The assertion `Scheduler stuck: no work scheduled but not finished` then aborts the process. When `max_minibatches` (`rinzler --max-batches`, `runtron --max-minibatches`) is above 0, the limit is at most `max_minibatches` times the maximum minibatch size.

evidence.quote: scheduled_everything, "Scheduler stuck: no work scheduled but not finished");

rows.name: TRON_LOG_DIR
rows.values: Path of a directory. The text is not checked. A relative path is relative to the current working directory.
rows.default: Unset: `alderaan.log` in the current working directory. For root the name is `alderaan-root.log`. Empty: `alderaan.log` in the current working directory, also for root.
rows.effect: The log file is `alderaan.log` in this directory, also for root. Output on stderr does not change. The file rotates at 512 MiB, and the code asks the log library for 3 rotated files.
rows.notes: When the log library cannot set up the file, the program prints `Log initialization failed` and exits with status 1. No command-line flag sets the directory. `TRON_LOG_LEVEL` sets the level of this file. Slice sets the variable to the run directory of each test.

rows.name: TRON_LOG_KV_GRANULARITY
rows.values: Integer number of bytes, parsed with `std::stoll`. Text after the leading number is ignored: `512MB` means 512 bytes. Text that does not start with a number terminates the process.
rows.default: Unset: 1073741824 bytes (1 GiB). Empty: `std::stoll` throws and the process terminates.
rows.effect: Sets how far the total KV cache size must change before the next info log line `KV cache footprint: <X> GB in <N> books` is written. A smaller value gives more log lines.
rows.notes: For text without a leading number, `std::stoll` throws at the first use, when the first KV book (one allocation of KV cache) is created. Nothing catches the exception. `0` or a negative number writes the line at every size update. The value is read once.

evidence.quote: spdlog::info("KV cache footprint: {:.2f} GB in {} books", new_gb, new_books);

new_terms.definition: The allocator `pos_heap_v2` for hugepage memory. It is the build default. `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR` selects between it and the legacy heap.
A table of the arena allocator with one record for each live allocation. The record holds the requested size and the caller addresses.
One run of the model over a group of tokens.
A group of tokens that one forward pass computes together. One forward pass can have several minibatches.
A mode of hardware attention in which one command handles a part of the attention heads in each pass over the K/V data.
A thread in rinzler and runtron that reads CPU temperature, CPU frequency and package power from `/sys`. It writes them to a Perfetto trace as counters of the category `hw`.
One Perfetto recording, from its start to its stop.
Running Average Power Limit. The CPU interface that reports energy use through files under `/sys/class/powercap`.
A counter that threads wait on during a forward pass.
The set of latches of one model state.
One allocation of KV cache storage. It holds a whole number of KV cache pages.

notes: All 12 rows kept, none dropped. Source code was opened for all 12 variables. TRON_HWATTN_COMPOUND_SPLIT is kept although it has no effect: product code still reads it. TRON_LOG_DIR: the row leaves out two facts that come from the spdlog source, which the checkout pins (cmake/versions.cmake:5, v1.17.0) but does not hold. In a local copy of spdlog v1.17.0, file_helper::open creates a missing directory before it opens the file, and the rotating sink keeps alderaan.1.log to alderaan.3.log next to alderaan.log (4 files, about 2 GiB). The input record of area cpp-pos-system says 'The directory must exist'. The spdlog copy contradicts that, so the row does not repeat it. TRON_LIVE_TOKEN_LIMIT: the abort for a value of 0 or less is derived by reading h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp (lines 2410, 2020-2025). It was not run. The field comment at full.hpp:1976 calls the limit soft ('can be exceeded in some cases'). The row does not say 'soft': every increment of n_live_tokens (lines 2461, 2552) follows a check against live_token_limit (lines 2410, 2543), so this code does not exceed the limit. TRON_HWATTN_EARLY_LAUNCH_MIN_B and TRON_LOG_KV_GRANULARITY: a bad value fails at first use, not in a startup check. The rows say 'at the first use' and do not claim that startup succeeds. Hardware sampler rows: rinzler_proxy links the code but has no call path to enable_hw_sampling, so read_by lists only rinzler and runtron. The four sampler rows are marked 'developers' (topic 'stats'); a support engineer who captures a trace may set TRON_HW_SAMPLER on advice. Evidence quotes hold no '|' character. Where the proving line holds '||' (src/pos/hwperf.cpp:128 and :186, src/system/memory.cpp:181, h/pos/device.hpp:806-807), the evidence cites the line next to it or the source comment that states the same rule.
